news.title: Hurricane Charity Scams Are Targeting Floridians — Here's How to Spot Them
news.excerpt: Hurricane season runs through November, and scammers know it. After every storm, fake charity websites, crowdfunding campaigns, and phone calls flood in — all pretending to help victims. They'll pressure you to donate right now. They'll ask for gift cards, wire transfers, or cryptocurrency. Real charities never ask for those. They'll use names that sound almost like real organizations (e.g., "Florida Hurricane Relief Fund" vs. the real "Florida Disaster Fund"). What to do: Before donating, verify the charity at ftc.gov/charity or guidestar.org. Pay by credit card only — it has fraud protection. If someone calls pushing for immediate payment, hang up.

news.title: That 'Microsoft Support' Call Is a Scam — Hang Up Immediately
news.excerpt: Your phone rings. The caller says they are from Microsoft or Windows Support. They claim your computer has a virus, a security problem, or an expired license — and they need remote access to fix it. Sometimes they ask for a credit card or gift cards to "renew" your protection.
